title: Why Sourcing Shifts Are Easier Said Than Done When Battling Tariffs
author: Supply Chain Dive Staff
full_text: New tariff pressure and geopolitical disruption are forcing manufacturers to reassess supplier networks, inventory buffers, and transportation lanes. Leaders are evaluating nearshoring strategies, supplier risk exposure, and faster planning cycles to protect margins and improve response time. Traditional visibility dashboards identify exposure, but teams still need decision workflows that recommend actions and coordinate execution.

title: 2026 Enterprise AI Predictions: Fragmentation, Commodification and the Agent Push Facing CIOs
author: InformationWeek Staff
full_text: Enterprise AI programs are shifting from analytics pilots toward automation, simulation, and decision intelligence. Supply chain leaders are prioritizing AI systems that detect demand volatility, evaluate alternatives, and recommend action before cost and service impacts escalate. The focus is moving away from generic dashboards and toward measurable outcomes.

title: Production Scheduling Is Broken, and It Needs to Change
author: Industry Week Staff
full_text: Manufacturing capacity constraints and labor shortages are affecting schedule compliance. Production planning teams are using digital manufacturing tools to detect bottlenecks, decide how to allocate scarce capacity, and do corrective actions faster. The business impact includes expedite costs, margin pressure, and delayed customer deliveries.
